outcome: The Agoh–Giuga conjecture itself (n prime iff pB_{p-1} ≡ -1 mod p) remains open, with no post-2024 change to the counterexample lower bound (still the 2013 Borwein–Maitland–Skerritt bound of 19,908 digits, itself pre-window). However, in 2026 an AI agent produced Lean-machine-checked proofs of two previously-open conjectures tightly bound up with the problem, listed on OEIS A309132 (the sequence whose 'a(n)=1 iff n prime' property is stated to be equivalent to Agoh-Giuga): (1) that this equivalence to Agoh-Giuga holds, and (2) that for composite n, a(n) is squarefree iff n is a Carmichael number (a 2019 Ordowski conjecture). Neither proof touches the truth value of Agoh-Giuga/A309132's primality conjecture itself, so the core problem is unmoved; the event is recorded as an instructive adjacent development.
credited_humans: Thomas Ordowski (2019, original squarefree/Carmichael conjecture statement)

ai.basis_quote: The proof that n is Carmichael iff n is composite and a(n) is squarefree was achieved by an autonomous AI agent, see the Tsoukalas paper and the Lean proof. ... Combining both directions yields the Carmichael equivalence (Summary by Opus 4.7).
ai.disclosed_cost: Paper's appendix records per-problem cost figures for this entry; WebFetch summaries of the PDF disagreed on the exact numbers across separate fetches (one pass reported $23 for the Agoh-Giuga-equivalence entry and $14 for the Carmichael/squarefree entry, both attributed to 'Claude Opus 4.8'; the OEIS comment itself credits a summary to 'Opus 4.7'). This inconsistency could not be resolved from a clean primary-text read of the PDF and is flagged as unverified rather than reported as fact.

summary: The frozen-revision statement of Agoh–Giuga is the primality biconditional pB_{p-1} ≡ -1 (mod p). This remains unproven and has no new counterexample-bound improvement since 26 January 2024 — the best bound (19,908 decimal digits / >10^19907, at least 4,771 prime factors) dates to Borwein, Maitland & Skerritt, 2013 (Zenodo record 10408952; also framed by some summaries as improving a 1996 bound), well before the window; the older Sorini 2001 figure of 10^36067 the triage found is likewise pre-window and in any case appears in some sources as a heuristic estimate rather than a rigorous bound, superseded by the 2013 rigorous result. In the window, the one genuine development is on OEIS sequence A309132, whose primality conjecture ('a(n)=1 iff n prime') is stated (informally, by Sondow/Ordowski circa 2019, and cited via Adamczewski 2026 on MathWorld) to be equivalent to Agoh-Giuga. As part of the 'OEIS Open' benchmark (Adamczewski, arXiv:2608.11941, submitted 12 Aug 2026, v2 13 Aug 2026), which tested language models against 492 previously-open OEIS conjectures formalized in Lean by Tsoukalas et al., an AI agent produced machine-checked Lean proofs of two claims tied to A309132: the equivalence-to-Agoh-Giuga framing, and the previously-conjectured (Ordowski, 2019) fact that for composite n, a(n) is squarefree iff n is a Carmichael number. Both are recorded on OEIS A309132 in a comment by Ralf Stephan dated 25 May 2026, crediting an 'autonomous AI agent' and a Lean proof, with a summary line crediting a Claude Opus variant. I treat this as `progress` rather than `partial`: the squarefree/Carmichael claim is a structural fact about A309132's denominators that narrows nothing about whether the Agoh-Giuga primality biconditional itself is true (a composite Agoh-Giuga counterexample was already known, pre-2024, to have to be a Carmichael number that is also a Giuga number — this is old Borwein-era knowledge; the new proof formalizes a related but not identical characterization of a(n)'s squarefreeness). Also, I could not independently verify with full confidence the exact AI model name and cost figures, because repeated attempts to read the arXiv PDF's raw text via WebFetch produced inconsistent numbers across passes (a symptom of that tool summarizing a dense compressed PDF rather than a clean extraction); I report what was found with that caveat rather than asserting a single number as fact. No arXiv preprint, journal paper, or lab announcement in the window claims to prove or refute Agoh-Giuga's core biconditional, or to improve the digit bound. Also noted in searching: two September 2025 Zenodo postings ('The Arithmetic Geometry of the Giuga Condition...') are self-labeled speculative AI-generated content ('a creative exploration of a concept with AI — it should not be taken as correct mathematics') and carry no mathematical weight; they are mentioned only because they surfaced in searches and could otherwise be mistaken for progress.
competing_reading: One could argue the A309132 result is `partial` progress on Agoh-Giuga rather than merely `progress`/adjacent, on the grounds that A309132's conjecture is stated by mathematicians to be *equivalent* to Agoh-Giuga, so proving facts about A309132's structure is proving facts 'about' Agoh-Giuga by proxy. I did not adopt this reading because neither of the two things actually proved is the equivalence's non-trivial direction bearing on primality itself: proving 'this is equivalent to Agoh-Giuga' is a reformulation, not new information about which n satisfy it, and the Carmichael/squarefree fact narrows the composite side of a related sequence's structure without deciding a single new case of 'n prime iff pB_{p-1}≡-1 mod p'. If a reader takes the equivalence relation itself as sufficient to fold any A309132 progress into Agoh-Giuga's own record, `partial` with `resolution_direction: confirmed` would be defensible instead.
what_would_settle_it: A primary, cleanly-extracted read of arXiv:2608.11941's full text and appendix table (rather than through a lossy PDF-to-text summarizer) to fix the exact system name, cost, and precise wording distinguishing what was newly proved versus previously known informally; and a statement from a number theorist on whether the A309132 Carmichael/squarefree proof is considered to bear on the Agoh-Giuga conjecture's open status.
